answer: Each identity must sail its claim through a canyon: a narrow channel admitting one identity at a time, taking one full epoch and leaving a public wake. The claim docks only in the harbor, a public anchorage open to any peer; a claim that never enters the harbor is ignored outright. The harbor admits claims only at high tide, when the whole passage is visible to all; a claim slipped in at low tide is turned away. A stranded claim — cargo not matching its wake — loses its berth and must sail the canyon again; ten voices need ten passages and ten high tides, and no passage can carry a clone.
